United Way of Greater Lehigh Valley, the local United Way that serves PPL’s headquarters community, nominated PPL for the honor. “At the PPL Foundation, we believe strong communities are built through collaboration and shared investment,” said Lissette Santana, President of the PPL Foundation. “Our partnership with United Way helps connect our employees’ generosity with trusted local organizations that are working every day to address critical needs and improve quality of life across the regions we serve.” PPL employees and retirees, together with matching contributions from PPL’s affiliated foundations, pledged $10 million during the company’s annual employee-led charitable giving campaign in 2025. These contributions support more than 500 local nonprofit organizations in communities served by PPL’s utilities in Kentucky, Pennsylvania and Rhode Island, with local United Ways helping to ensure funds are directed to areas of greatest need. “Welcoming PPL into United Way Worldwide’s Leading Corporate Partner program is a milestone and a reflection of the extraordinary partnership we have built,” said Caitlin Wagner, Senior Director, Global Corporate Partnership and Development, United Way Worldwide. “The recognition reflects decades of collaboration, shared purpose, and meaningful investment in creating stronger, more resilient communities – both in Greater Lehigh Valley where PPL is based – and across the country.” “PPL exemplifies community leadership in every way. When our communities are in crisis or our residents need support, we know that we can count on the team at PPL. We are so grateful for their years of partnership and trust, and we will continue to create real impact in the communities we serve together,” added Marci Lesko, President and Chief Executive Officer, United Way of the Greater Lehigh Valley. PPL’s partnership with United Way is deeply rooted. Each year, more than 1,000 PPL employees also volunteer during United Way’s Day of Caring. July 23, 2026

title: Cyber Deception with Koney and Dynatrace
summary: Deploy automated honeytokens in Kubernetes with Koney: set traps for attackers, detect file access with eBPF and Tetragon, and forward alerts to Dynatrace.
body_text: Deploy automated honeytokens in Kubernetes with Koney: set traps for attackers, detect file access with eBPF and Tetragon, and forward alerts to Dynatrace. Imagine an attacker has breached your perimeter. They’ve gained access to a container in your Kubernetes cluster and are now searching through the file system, looking for secrets (credentials, tokens, keys) that they can use to further the attack. What if those secrets were fake? What if, the moment the attacker attempts to read a fake credential, you get an alert? That’s the idea behind honeytokens: small, realistic-looking files placed in strategic locations to catch unauthorized access attempts. When someone touches them, you may have a very strong indicator of compromise (IoC) that warrants investigation because legitimate users would never interact with these decoys. In this blog post, we introduce Koney , an open source research project that integrates seamlessly with Dynatrace. Koney is a Kubernetes operator that automates the deployment of honeytokens across your cluster. We’ll walk through the setup from scratch: installing Koney, writing your first deception policy, watching it scale across containers, and forwarding alerts directly to Dynatrace. What is Koney? Koney is a Kubernetes operator developed by the cloud-native security research team at Dynatrace, together with Matteo Golinelli from the University of Trento. It lets you define deception policies that describe which traps to deploy, where to deploy them, and how to monitor them. Currently, the open source version of Koney supports placing honeytokens in the file system. You can download or contribute on GitHub . Why cyber deception? Traditional security approaches focus on building walls and closing gaps: scanning for vulnerabilities with Runtime Vulnerability Analytics (RVA) , blocking attacks in real-time with Runtime Application Protection (RAP) , and fixing misconfigurations with Security Posture Management (SPM) . These are all essential. But they share a common limitation: defenders must close every hole, while attackers need to find just one . With the rise of Generative AI , this asymmetry is getting worse. Attackers can increasingly use AI-assisted tools and automation to accelerate portions of the attack lifecycle. Instead of trying to keep attackers out, cyber deception places traps on the inside. Now, the attacker, whether human or automated, must watch their steps to not trigger an alert. Honeytokens are one of the simplest deception techniques. Unlike noisy intrusion detection systems, a honeytoken generates a signal only when something truly suspicious happens: properly configured legitimate processes generally should not access a decoy credentials file planted by your security team. Deception has a rich history in information security. Researchers like Lance Spitzner popularized the concept of honeypots in the early 2000s. Academic research has demonstrated that deception techniques can help detect and slow attacker activity in specific scenarios. But widespread industry adoption has been held back by the operational burden: manually creating, deploying, monitoring, and rotating honeytokens across dozens of containers is tedious and error prone. Koney solves this by letting you express your deception strategy as a Kubernetes custom resource (a DeceptionPolicy object) and handling everything else automatically. Using Koney for deception When you apply a DeceptionPolicy , Koney: Deploys the trap (the “decoy”) by mounting a volume or executing a shell command in the container. Sets up monitoring (the “captor”) using Tetragon’s eBPF-based tracing policies to detect file access. Collects alerts , logging them and optionally forwarding them to external systems like Dynatrace. When you update a policy, Koney updates the traps. When you delete a policy, Koney removes them. When you spawn new pods that match the policy, Koney automatically deploys traps there too. It’s deception-as-code for Kubernetes. Walkthrough: Honeytokens with Koney and Dynatrace For this walkthrough, you’ll need: A Kubernetes cluster. kubectl installed and connected to your cluster. helm , to install Koney and Tetragon. Step 1: Install Koney Install Koney with Helm in the koney-system namespace: helm install koney --create-namespace -n koney-system --wait oci://ghcr.io/dynatrace-oss/koney/charts/koney --version 0.2.1 Verify that the Koney controller is running: kubectl wait --for=condition=ready pod -n koney-system -l control-plane=controller-manager That’s it. Koney is now watching for DeceptionPolicy custom resources in your cluster. Step 2: Install Tetragon Koney uses Tetragon for eBPF-based monitoring. Tetragon watches for file access events at the kernel level. Add the Cilium Helm repository and install Tetragon: helm repo add cilium https://helm.cilium.io helm repo update helm install tetragon cilium/tetragon -n kube-system --set dnsPolicy=ClusterFirstWithHostNet The dnsPolicy=ClusterFirstWithHostNet setting is required so that Tetragon can resolve the addresses of Koney’s internal services to forward alerts. If you have Tetragon already installed, make sure to set this option. Verify that Tetragon is running: kubectl get pods -n kube-system -l app.kubernetes.io/name=tetragon Step 3: Deploy a sample application To see Koney in action, we need an application running in the cluster. Create and apply a demo-app.yaml manifest with label honeytoken: “ true ” set in the pod labels. Alternatively, you can also use any existing application in your cluster; just make sure the relevant pods carry the label honeytoken=true. We’ll use this in our deception policy to select which containers get honeytokens. # demo-app.yaml apiVersion : apps/v1 kind : Deployment metadata : name : demo-app spec : selector : matchLabels : app : demo-app template : metadata : labels : app : demo-app ho n ey t o k en : "true" spec : containers : - name : nginx image : nginx kubectl apply -f demo-app.yaml At this point, there are no honeytokens in the container. Let’s verify that: kubectl exec -it deploy/demo-app -- ls /run/secrets/ You’ll only see the standard Kubernetes service account token but no traps … yet. Step 4: Write a DeceptionPolicy A DeceptionPolicy is a custom resource that describes what to deploy and where. We’ll place a decoy credentials file at /run/secrets/.aws/credentials . This is a common path that attackers look for when hunting for cloud provider secrets. Credential files in well-known paths are among the first things attackers look for after gaining a foothold. Here’s the full policy: # ho n ey t o k en .yaml apiVersion : research.dynatr ac e.com/v1alpha1 kind : DeceptionPolicy metadata : name : aws - cred e n t ial s -trap spec : strictValidation : true mutateExisting : true traps : - filesystem Ho n ey t o k en : filePath : /run/secrets/. aws / cred e n t ial s readOnly : true fileContent : | [default] aws_ ac cess_key_id = FZWGQYZRVMVQKCWXWJ aws_secret_ ac cess_key = ToDNS2V5wkEuPmfocmNDHiVBspaywo region = us-east-1 [staging] aws_ ac cess_key_id = BPDHLBUJTYMKRVBMNB aws_secret_ ac cess_key = Jf4mTvTG5zbLksf464nYwEVyDkbjdp region = eu-central-1 [prod] aws_ ac cess_key_id = GQRMYWAXADTVUPFMZJ aws_secret_ ac cess_key = gUFQzyJWJSkMkWpay4Umxzg4oFkkju region = us-east-1 match : any : - resources : selector : matchLabels : ho n ey t o k en : "true" decoyDeployment : strategy : containerExec captorDeployment : strategy : tetragon Let’s break this down: filesystemHoneytoken defines the trap type and sets path and content for a realistic credentials file. match tells Koney which containers should receive this trap. Here, we target any pod with the label honeytoken : “ true “. You can also match by namespace, container name, and more. The full matching syntax is documented in Koney’s documentation file. decoyDeployment defines how the trap is placed. The containerExec strategy injects the file by running a shell command inside the container. Koney also supports other strategies, such as volumeMount , which mounts a Kubernetes volume instead. captorDeployment defines how the trap is monitored. The tetragon strategy creates a Tetragon TracingPolicy to detect file access using eBPF. Apply the policy: kubectl apply -f honeytoken.yaml Step 5: Verify the deployment Koney should have deployed the honeytoken within seconds. First, let’s look at the policy status: kubectl describe deceptionpolicy aws-credentials-trap In the status conditions, you should see that the policy was found and both the decoy and captor have been deployed successfully. Now, let’s look inside the container: kubectl exec -it deploy/demo-app -- cat /run/secrets/.aws/credentials You should see the decoy AWS credentials we defined. This file was injected by Koney; it wasn’t in the original container image. An attacker stumbling onto this file would see what looks like valid credentials and try to use them. The moment they read the file, an alert is already triggered. Scales automatically, stays transparent The deception policy applies to all matching containers. If you add new workloads or scale up your deployment, every new pod also automatically receives the honeytoken. This is one of the key advantages of expressing deception “as code.” Let’s test it by scaling up our deployment: kubectl scale deployment demo-app --replicas=3 Koney also tracks what it deployed using a koney/changes annotation. Let’s inspect it: kubectl get pod -l app=demo-app -o jsonpath="{.items[0].metadata.annotations['koney/changes']}" | jq You should see something like this: [ { " deceptionPolicyName " : " aws - cred e n t ial s -trap" , "traps" : [ { " deploymentStrategy " : " containerExec " , "containers" : [ "nginx" ] , " createdAt " : "2026-03-27T15:24:26Z" , " updatedAt " : "2026-03-27T15:26:18Z" , " filesystem Ho n ey t o k en " : { " filePath " : "/run/secrets/. aws / cred e n t ial s " , " fileContentHash " : "feb7302a35b1031040d1151c6cc5c9f7" , " readOnly " : true } } ] } ] Step 6: Trigger an alert Now let’s simulate an attacker finding and reading the honeytoken. Open a shell in the container and access the honeytoken: kubectl exec -it deploy/demo-app -- bash $ cd /run/secrets/.aws $ ls -ll $ cat cred e n t ial s To see the alert, check the logs of the Koney alerts container: kubectl logs -n koney -system -l control-plane=controller-manager -c alerts -f --since 1h | jq You’ll see a JSON alert with rich context: { "timestamp" : "2026-03-27T15:24:43Z" , " deception_policy_name " : " aws - cred e n t ial s -trap" , " trap_type " : " filesystem_ ho n ey t o k en " , "metadata" : { " file_path " : "/run/secrets/. aws / cred e n t ial s " }, "pod" : { "name" : "demo-app-68ff4cbb88-4bxbx" , "namesp ac e" : "default" , "container" : { "id" : "a28a42618599..." , "name" : "nginx" } }, "node" : { "name" : "ip-10-20-30-40.ec2.internal" }, "process" : { " uid " : 0 , " pid " : 1061063 , " cwd " : "/" , "binary" : "/ usr /bin/cat" , "arguments" : "/run/secrets/. aws / cred e n t ial s " } } This tells you ex ac tly where the ac cess happened (pod, namesp ac e, container), w ho did it (process binary, PID, UID), and which policy was triggered. Step 7: Forward alerts to Dynatrace Seeing alerts in logs is fine for testing, but in production, you’ll want them in your security platform. Koney supports forwarding alerts to Dynatrace using a DeceptionAlertSink resource. To set this up, you’ll need a Dynatrace API token and environment URL stored in a Kubernetes secret. The detailed instructions for creating the token with the correct scopes are in Koney’s documentation on alert sinks . Once you have the secret, create a DeceptionAlertSink (assuming your secret is named dynatrace-api-token ): # dynatr ac e-sink.yaml apiVersion : research.dynatr ac e.com/v1alpha1 kind : DeceptionAlertSink metadata : name : deceptionalertsink-dynatr ac e namesp ac e : koney -system spec : dynatr ac e : secretName : dynatr ac e - api -token severity : HIGH Apply it: kubectl apply -f dynatr ac e-sink.yaml When configured successfully, honeytoken access alerts can be forwarded to Dynatrace as security events . See it in Dynatrace After setting up the alert sink, trigger a few more access events to generate findings in Dynatrace: kubectl exec -it deploy/demo-app -- cat /run/secrets/.aws/credentials Then open the Threats & Exploits app in Dynatrace. You’ll see the detection findings with all the contextual information. Koney alerts in the Threats & Exploits app Each finding includes structured fields like koney.deception_policy_name , koney.trap_type , k8s.pod.name , and process.executable.name . This means you can write Dynatrace Query Language (DQL) queries to further analyze and correlate events with Investigations . fetch security.events | filter event.provider == "Koney" Koney alerts in the Notebooks app Step 8: Update and remove policies One of the most practical benefits of Koney is that deception policies are living resources. You can update them at any time. Try changing the fileContent field in your honeytoken.yaml and re-apply the policy: kubectl apply -f honeytoken.yaml Koney will update the honeytoken across all matching containers. This enables dynamic deception strategies. When you’re done, delete the policy: kubectl delete -f honeytoken.yaml Koney automatically cleans up all deployed honeytokens from every container. What’s next Koney currently supports filesystem honeytokens, but the project is designed to support additional deception techniques in future versions. including deceptive HTTP endpoints and payloads that can lure vulnerability scanners and redirect them to honeypots. Once alerts are flowing into Dynatrace, the possibilities go further. For example, you could build a Workflow that triggers on Koney alerts, looks up the owner of the affected namespace using the Ownership app, and creates a ticket for the security team. We previously demonstrated this kind of end-to-end security automation in the blog post, Context-aware security incident response with Dynatrace Automations and Tetragon , but now with Koney, even more steps are automated. If you’re interested in the research behind Koney, we recommend reading the Koney paper , published in the 4th Workshop on Active Defense and Deception (AD&D), co-located with the 10th IEEE European Symposium on Security and Privacy (EuroS&P ’25).

title: POSCO AIR SOLUTION Completes High-Purity Rare Gas Plant, Enhancing Domestic Supply Chain Stability through Localization of Key Materials for Semiconductor and Aerospace Industries
summary: Posco Newsroom
body_text: POSCO Air Solution Completes High-Purity Rare Gas Plant, Enhancing Domestic Supply Chain Stability through Localization of Key Materials for Semiconductor and Aerospace Industries 2026/06/22 Mail facebook twitter linkedin Completion of high-purity rare gas plant at the Gwangyang Donghoan site… Full-scale entry into next-generation semiconductor and aerospace-related industries Producing high-purity xenon, krypton, and neon with an annual capacity of 130,000 Nm³… Capable of meeting 52% of domestic semiconductor demand POSCO Group accelerates industrial gas business… Expanding specialty gas portfolio in synergy with steelmaking operations POSCO Group has completed the construction of a high-purity rare gas plant for the semiconductor and aerospace industries, further strengthening its competitiveness in next-generation businesses linked with its steelmaking operations. POSCO Air Solution (CEO Kim Dae-yeon), an industrial gas affiliate of POSCO Group, held a completion ceremony for its high-purity rare gas plant at the Donghoan site of Gwangyang Works on the 17th. Held in conjunction with the Electric Arc Furnace (EAF) completion ceremony, the event was attended by approximately 100 guests, including Chang In-hwa, CEO of POSCO Holdings, government officials, local government representatives, and executives and employees of client and partner companies. POSCO Air Solution produces high-purity products using rare gases extracted from POSCO’s oxygen plants as feedstock. Recognizing the growing importance of rare gases in the semiconductor and aerospace sectors, POSCO established a dedicated new business organization in 2021 and expanded it into the Industrial Gas Business Division in 2023 to systematically prepare for market entry. The completion of this plant enables the localization of key materials for semiconductors and aerospace that were previously entirely import-dependent, which is expected to significantly enhance supply chain stability across the nation’s advanced industries. The newly completed plant has an annual production capacity of 130,000 Normal cubic meters (Nm³)*, capable of meeting approximately 52% of the domestic semiconductor industry’s demand for rare gases. The facility refines crude gas extracted from the oxygen plants of POSCO’s steelworks into high-purity xenon (Xe), krypton (Kr), and neon (Ne). These rare gases are essential materials widely used across advanced industries, including semiconductor lithography and etching processes, as well as aerospace and medical applications. *Note: Normal cubic meter (Nm³) is a unit used for flow rate and volume, where “N” stands for “Normal,” representing standard conditions (typically 0°C and 1 atm), and m³ represents the volume under actual operating conditions. In his commemorative speech, POSCO Holdings CEO Chang In-hwa stated, “Amid intensifying instability in global supply chains for key materials, it is highly meaningful that we can now directly produce and stably supply essential materials for advanced industries that will shape the nation’s future, such as semiconductors and aerospace, using our own technology.” He added, “This milestone goes beyond merely building a factory; it will serve as a reliable pillar safeguarding the supply chain security of South Korea’s advanced industries.” With the completion of the high-purity rare gas plant, POSCO Group plans to expand its portfolio into various specialty gas businesses in synergy with its steelmaking operations. By combining POSCO’s world-class steelmaking infrastructure with its advanced gas purification technology, the company aims to not only supply the oxygen and nitrogen required for the production of steel and rechargeable battery materials but also lead the high-value-added rare and specialty gas markets. ▲ On the 17th, POSCO Air Solution held a completion ceremony for its high-purity rare gas plant. (From left) Lee Jong-geun, President of Hanyang ENG; Jeon Hyeong-yeol, Director of the Korea Aerospace Research Institute (KARI); Woo Kwang-il, Chairman of the Gwangyang Chamber of Commerce and Industry; Jeong Tae-seong, Director General of the Yeosu Regional Office of Oceans and Fisheries; Lee Hee-geun, President of POSCO; Jeong In-hwa, Gwangyang Mayor; Chang In-hwa, CEO of POSCO Holdings; Zhang Yuchun, President of Zhongtai; Wu Zhangmin, Director of Weihua Group; Park Seong-hyeon, Gwangyang Mayor-elect; Shin Seong-won, Head of POSCO Corporate Planning Headquarters; and Kim Dae-yeon, President of POSCO Air Solution. ▲ On the 17th, Chang In-hwa, CEO of POSCO Holdings, delivers a commemorative speech at the completion ceremony of the high-purity rare gas plant. ▲ Lee Hee-geun, President of POSCO; Park Seong-hyeon, Gwangyang Mayor-elect; Chang In-hwa, CEO of POSCO Holdings; and Jeong In-hwa, Gwangyang Mayor, inspect the POSCO Air Solution high-purity rare gas plant. high purity rare gas POSCO Air Solution

title: Web search
summary: A new web search API is now available in Ollama. Ollama provides a generous free tier of web searches for individuals to use, and higher rate limits are available via Ollama’s cloud.
body_text:
A new web search API is now available in Ollama. Ollama provides a generous free tier of web searches for individuals to use, and higher rate limits are available via Ollama’s cloud . This web search capability can augment models with the latest information from the web to reduce hallucinations and improve accuracy. Web search is provided as a REST API with deeper tool integrations in Ollama’s Python and JavaScript libraries. This also enables models such as OpenAI’s gpt-oss models to conduct long-running research tasks. Get started Create an API key from your Ollama account . export OLLAMA_API_KEY="your_api_key" cURL curl https://ollama.com/api/web_search \ --header "Authorization: Bearer $OLLAMA_API_KEY" \ -d '{ "query": "what is ollama?" }' Example output { "results": [ { "title": "Ollama", "url": "https://ollama.com/", "content": "Cloud models are now available..." }, { "title": "What is Ollama? Introduction to the AI model management tool", "url": "https://www.hostinger.com/tutorials/what-is-ollama", "content": "Ariffud M. 6min Read..." }, { "title": "Ollama Explained: Transforming AI Accessibility and Language ...", "url": "https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/artificial-intelligence/ollama-explained-transforming-ai-accessibility-and-language-processing/", "content": "Data Science Data Science Projects Data Analysis..." } ] } Python Install and run Ollama’s Python library pip install 'ollama>=0.6.0' Then make a request using ollama.web_search : import ollama response = ollama.web_search("What is Ollama?") print(response) Example output results = [ { "title": "Ollama", "url": "https://ollama.com/", "content": "Cloud models are now available in Ollama..." }, { "title": "What is Ollama? Features, Pricing, and Use Cases - Walturn", "url": "https://www.walturn.com/insights/what-is-ollama-features-pricing-and-use-cases", "content": "Our services..." }, { "title": "Complete Ollama Guide: Installation, Usage & Code Examples", "url": "https://collabnix.com/complete-ollama-guide-installation-usage-code-examples", "content": "Join our Discord Server..." } ] JavaScript Install and run Ollama’s JavaScript library npm install 'ollama@>=0.6.0' import { Ollama } from "ollama"; const client = new Ollama(); const results = await client.webSearch({ query: "what is ollama?" }); console.log(JSON.stringify(results, null, 2)); Example output { "results": [ { "title": "Ollama", "url": "https://ollama.com/", "content": "Cloud models are now available..." }, { "title": "What is Ollama? Introduction to the AI model management tool", "url": "https://www.hostinger.com/tutorials/what-is-ollama", "content": "Ollama is an open-source tool..." }, { "title": "Ollama Explained: Transforming AI Accessibility and Language Processing", "url": "https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/artificial-intelligence/ollama-explained-transforming-ai-accessibility-and-language-processing/", "content": "Ollama is a groundbreaking..." } ] } Building a search agent Use Ollama’s web search as a tool to build a mini search agent. The example uses Alibaba’s Qwen 3 model with 4B parameters. ollama pull qwen3:4b from ollama import chat, web_fetch, web_search available_tools = {'web_search': web_search, 'web_fetch': web_fetch} messages = [{'role': 'user', 'content': "what is ollama's new engine"}] while True: response = chat( model='qwen3:4b', messages=messages, tools=[web_search, web_fetch], think=True ) if response.message.thinking: print('Thinking: ', response.message.thinking) if response.message.content: print('Content: ', response.message.content) messages.append(response.message) if response.message.tool_calls: print('Tool calls: ', response.message.tool_calls) for tool_call in response.message.tool_calls: function_to_call = available_tools.get(tool_call.function.name) if function_to_call: args = tool_call.function.arguments result = function_to_call(**args) print('Result: ', str(result)[:200]+'...') # Result is truncated for limited context lengths messages.append({'role': 'tool', 'content': str(result)[:2000 * 4], 'tool_name': tool_call.function.name}) else: messages.append({'role': 'tool', 'content': f'Tool {tool_call.function.name} not found', 'tool_name': tool_call.function.name}) else: break Result Thinking: Okay, the user is asking about Ollama's new engine. I need to figure out what they're referring to. Ollama is a company that develops large language models, so maybe they've released a new model or an updated version of their existing engine... Tool calls: [ToolCall(function=Function(name='web_search', arguments={'max_results': 3, 'query': 'Ollama new engine'}))] Result: results=[WebSearchResult(content='# New model scheduling

## September 23, 2025

Ollama now includes a significantly improved model scheduling system. Ahead of running a model, Ollama’s new engine... Thinking: Okay, the user asked about Ollama's new engine. Let me look at the search results. First result is from September 23, 2025, talking about new model scheduling. It mentions improved memory management, reduced crashes, better GPU utilization, and multi-GPU performance. Examples show speed improvements and accurate memory reporting. Supported models include gemma3, llama4, qwen3, etc... Content: Ollama has introduced two key updates to its engine, both released in 2025: 1. **Enhanced Model Scheduling (September 23, 2025)** - **Precision Memory Management**: Exact memory allocation reduces out-of-memory crashes and optimizes GPU utilization. - **Performance Gains**: Examples show significant speed improvements (e.g., 85.54 tokens/s vs 52.02 tokens/s) and full GPU layer utilization. - **Multi-GPU Support**: Improved efficiency across multiple GPUs, with accurate memory reporting via tools like `nvidia-smi`. - **Supported Models**: Includes `gemma3`, `llama4`, `qwen3`, `mistral-small3.2`, and more. 2. **Multimodal Engine (May 15, 2025)** - **Vision Support**: First-class support for vision models, including `llama4:scout` (109B parameters), `gemma3`, `qwen2.5vl`, and `mistral-small3.1`. - **Multimodal Tasks**: Examples include identifying animals in multiple images, answering location-based questions from videos, and document scanning. These updates highlight Ollama's focus on efficiency, performance, and expanded capabilities for both text and vision tasks. Recommended models: These models have great tool-use capabilities and are able to have multi-turn interactions with the user and tools to get to a final result. qwen3 gpt-oss Recommended cloud models: qwen3:480b-cloud gpt-oss:120b-cloud deepseek-v3.1-cloud The web_search and web_fetch tools can return thousands of tokens. It is recommended to increase the context length of the model to ~32000 tokens for reasonable performance. Search agents work best with full context length. Fetching page results To fetch individual pages (e.g. when a user provides a url in the prompt), use the new web fetch API. Python library from ollama import web_fetch result = web_fetch('https://ollama.com') print(result) Result WebFetchResponse( title='Ollama', content='[Cloud models](https://ollama.com/blog/cloud-models) are now available in Ollama

**Chat & build with open models**

[Download](https://ollama.com/download) [Explore models](https://ollama.com/models)

Available for macOS, Windows, and Linux', links=['https://ollama.com/', 'https://ollama.com/models', 'https://github.com/ollama/ollama'] ) Example Python code is available on GitHub . JavaScript library import { Ollama } from "ollama"; const client = new Ollama(); const fetchResult = await client.webFetch({ url: "https://ollama.com" }); console.log(JSON.stringify(fetchResult, null, 2)); Result { "title": "Ollama", "content": "[Cloud models](https://ollama.com/blog/cloud-models) are now available in Ollama...", "links": [ "https://ollama.com/", "https://ollama.com/models", "https://github.com/ollama/ollama" ] } Example JavaScript code is available on GitHub . cURL curl --request POST \ --url https://ollama.com/api/web_fetch \ --header "Authorization: Bearer $OLLAMA_API_KEY" \ --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --data '{ "url": "ollama.com" }' Result { "title": "Ollama", "content": "[Cloud models](https://ollama.com/blog/cloud-models) are now available in Ollama...", "links": [ "http://ollama.com/", "http://ollama.com/models", "https://github.com/ollama/ollama" ] } Integrations MCP Server (Model Context Protocol server) You can enable web search in any MCP client through the Python MCP server . Cline To integrate with Cline, configure MCP servers in its settings. Manage MCP Servers > Configure MCP Servers > Add the configuration below { "mcpServers": { "web_search_and_fetch": { "type": "stdio", "command": "uv", "args": ["run", "path/to/web-search-mcp.py"], "env": { "OLLAMA_API_KEY": "your_api_key_here" } } } } Codex Add the following configuration to ~/.codex/config.toml [mcp_servers.web_search] command = "uv" args = ["run", "path/to/web-search-mcp.py"] env = { "OLLAMA_API_KEY" = "your_api_key_here" } Goose You can integrate with Ollama via Goose’s extensions. Get started Web search is included with a free Ollama account, with much higher rate limits available by upgrading your Ollama subscription . To get started, sign up for an Ollama account !

title: A Comprehensive Guide to Finance Automation Process and Benefits
summary: All-in-one Spend Management platform for Procure-to-Pay, Corporate Cards, Accounts Payable Automation, Vendor Payouts, Reimbursements and more!
body_text: Managing financial workflows manually is becoming a significant challenge for businesses as they scale. Errors, inefficiencies, and time-consuming processes can hinder growth and decision-making. A recent survey shows that 51% of Indian organisations report that employees are eager to work with new AI and automation tools, highlighting the increasing demand for digital solutions in finance. Finance automation is no longer a nice-to-have. It simplifies complex workflows, reduces manual effort, improves accuracy, and helps teams stay compliant as they scale. In this blog, we’ll break down what finance automation really means, the key processes it improves, common pitfalls to avoid, and how to start building an automation strategy that works. TL;DR: Finance automation streamlines tasks like procurement, invoice processing, and reporting, reducing manual effort and errors. It enables better cash flow management by automating payments, approvals, and reconciliations. Accurate, real-time data through system integrations improves decision-making and compliance. Custom workflows and rule-based automations help scale finance operations without increasing headcount. Successful automation requires clear planning, clean data, employee training, and continuous monitoring. What is Finance Automation? Finance automation refers to the use of technology to streamline and automate various finance-related tasks and processes. In modern businesses, financial automation is essential for enhancing operational efficiency, minimising errors, and ensuring compliance. Automation involves the use of software systems to handle tasks that were traditionally done manually, such as invoice processing, procurement, accounts payable (AP), vendor payments, and financial reporting. The scope of finance automation in today’s businesses spans across several critical financial functions, enabling greater accuracy, efficiency, and cost savings. Procurement : Automating purchase requests, purchase orders, and vendor management. Accounts Payable : Automating invoice processing, approvals, and payments. Vendor Payments : Streamlining payments to vendors, ensuring timely processing. Expense Management : Automating employee expense claims, approval workflows, and reimbursements. Financial Reporting : Automating the generation of financial reports, making it easier to track performance and ensure compliance. Compliance & Taxation : Automating tax calculations and regulatory reporting ensures businesses stay compliant without manual effort. Manual Finance Processes vs. Automated Systems Manual financial operations might work in the early days, but they quickly become roadblocks as a business scales. Errors, delays, and limited visibility make it harder to move fast or stay compliant. Here’s how automation changes the game: Manual Processes Automated Systems Prone to errors due to manual data entry Minimises human error through automated data entry and validation Time-consuming, requiring multiple steps for approvals and processing Reduces processing time and speeds up approvals with automation Limited visibility into spend or financial performance in real time Enables real-time visibility into spend, invoices, and vendor payments Higher risk of non-compliance due to manual tracking and errors Helps ensure compliance with tax laws and accounting standards automatically For growing businesses, automation is essential for staying competitive and improving profitability. Understanding its core components is key to building efficient financial operations. Key Components of the Finance Automation Process Finance automation covers a wide range of processes, each contributing to smoother workflows, better cash flow management, and more accurate reporting. Let’s dive deeper into the key components of the finance automation process: Procurement Automation: Automates the full purchase cycle from digital requests and approval workflows to vendor selection and PO generation. This reduces delays, prevents maverick spend, and improves vendor compliance. Invoice Processing: Simplifies invoice capture, matching, and approval routing. By eliminating manual data entry and automating payment scheduling, teams reduce errors and avoid late fees. Accounts Payable & Receivable: Streamlines outgoing and incoming payments. Scheduled disbursements, automatic reconciliations, and collection reminders help maintain positive cash flow and reduce finance workload. Expense Management: Digitises employee reimbursements with automated policy checks, approvals, and payment processing. This improves compliance, speeds up reimbursements, and reduces friction for employees. Financial Reporting: Generates real-time reports and dashboards using data directly from integrated systems. This gives finance leaders accurate, up-to-date insights without manual number crunching. Compliance & Taxation: Handles tax calculations, audit trails, and local compliance checks automatically. Ensures timely filings and reduces regulatory risk with minimal manual oversight. With the key components in place, it’s important to understand how to implement them through a structured automation process. Steps in the Finance Automation Process Implementing finance automation involves a series of practical steps that guide businesses from manual processes to fully streamlined operations. 1. Assessment & Planning Most businesses begin automation with an internal audit, but the mistake many make is stopping at surface-level inefficiencies. For companies dealing with high invoice volumes, delayed approvals, or duplicate vendor entries, it's crucial to map out not just what tasks are repetitive, but where manual interventions cause revenue leaks or compliance risks. For example, are vendor payouts delayed due to back-and-forth email approvals? Or are purchase requests getting lost across teams? Documenting these patterns helps prioritise automation where it truly matters. This stage should also align goals, like reducing processing time, eliminating manual errors, or improving audit readiness. 2. Choosing the Right Tools & Platform The wrong tool can make finance automation feel more complicated than doing things manually. For businesses managing procurement and payouts, it’s not enough for software to simply process invoices. It also needs to support approvals, track vendor relationships, and keep data accurate across departments. This is where platforms like Kodo stand out, offering an all-in-one solution that eliminates the need for multiple disconnected tools. Kodo empowers finance teams with: Automated Purchase Requests : Streamline how teams request and initiate purchases. Invoice Workflow Automation : Reduce manual invoice processing with built-in logic. Custom Approval Workflows : Set multi-level, rule-based approvals tailored to your org structure. Vendor Payout Automation : Automate and track vendor payments with accuracy and speed. Real-Time Spend Visibility : Monitor spending trends and control budgets across departments. Additionally, Kodo is ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certified , ensuring enterprise-grade data security and compliance for all your financial operations. 3. Workflow Design & Customisation One of the most significant ICP pain points is that finance workflows often involve cross-functional dependencies—procurement requests need budget holder approvals, invoices need matching with POs, and vendor payments must align with compliance rules. Off-the-shelf automation can't capture these nuances. That’s why businesses must tailor workflows to reflect their internal hierarchy, risk checks, and approval thresholds. For instance, automating approvals for software renewals under ₹50,000 while routing larger purchases to department heads ensures both speed and control. Customising these flows also reduces friction between finance and other teams. 4. Data Integration Without clean data, automation fails. Finance teams often rely on fragmented systems such as ERP software , bank portals, and spreadsheets. These silos lead to mismatches and errors. Integrating automation tools with ERP platforms, banking APIs, and vendor databases enables accurate, real-time data syncing across the payment lifecycle. 5. Automation Setup & Testing This phase often breaks down when rushed. Implementing automation without sandbox testing can lead to incorrect payouts or approval gaps. Setting up conditional rules, such as auto-approving recurring software bills or flagging GST mismatches, requires careful calibration. Testing should simulate real scenarios: How does the system handle missing vendor info? What happens if a purchase exceeds the budget mid-process? Resolving these cases early ensures the automation works reliably under actual business pressure. 6. Employee Training A common reason automation fails is user resistance. When procurement or finance teams don’t understand the new workflow or distrust the data, they fall back on manual workarounds. Training must go beyond tool usage. Teams need to understand the purpose behind the automation, how it eases their workload, and what governance is built into the system. 7. Monitoring & Continuous Improvement Automation isn’t a "set-and-forget" solution. Businesses should track metrics like invoice cycle time, payment accuracy, or approval lag per department. If approvals consistently stall at a specific level, that’s a workflow design flaw. If vendors complain about delayed payments despite automation, there might be a data sync issue. Following these steps ensures a smooth transition to automated finance operations. This paves the way for significant improvements in efficiency and accuracy. Benefits of Finance Automation Finance automation delivers powerful advantages that streamline operations, reduce costs, and enhance accuracy across financial processes. 1. Increased Efficiency Manual finance tasks—like invoice matching, chasing approvals, or processing vendor payouts—consume valuable time and delay operations. Automation eliminates these repetitive steps by routing approvals, flagging mismatches, and executing scheduled payments without human intervention. 2. Improved Accuracy Finance teams often deal with errors caused by duplicate data entry, mismatched POs, or missing vendor details. These mistakes not only disrupt payments but also affect trust with suppliers. 3. Cost Savings Businesses relying on manual workflows often incur hidden costs, including staff hours, late payment penalties, and the expense of maintaining paper trails. Automation significantly cuts these costs by reducing FTE hours spent on mundane tasks and avoiding fees from delayed filings or approvals. Over time, this leads to more predictable operational spending and leaner finance operations. 4. Better Cash Flow Management For companies dealing with multiple vendors, staggered payment terms, and variable approval cycles, managing cash flow can feel chaotic. Finance automation enables scheduled, rule-based payments and real-time visibility into payable cycles. For instance, recurring software subscriptions or contract-based payouts can be automated with alerts before due dates, ensuring cash isn’t locked up unnecessarily and vendors are paid on time. 5. Enhanced Compliance & Risk Management Late tax filings, missed audit trails, or non-compliant vendor contracts can expose businesses to regulatory fines. Automated platforms embed rules that ensure timely payments, GST-compliant invoicing, and audit-ready logs for every financial transaction. 6. Real-time Financial Visibility Manual processes often delay reporting, leaving leadership with outdated financial data. Automation provides a real-time dashboard of payables, pending approvals, and spending across departments. This provides CFOs and finance leaders with actionable insights for informed strategic decisions, whether it's negotiating vendor terms, reallocating budgets, or forecasting future expenditures. 7. Scalability As businesses grow, so does the complexity of managing more vendors, invoices, and internal approval structures. Finance automation helps scale operations without scaling headcount. Workflows can be easily replicated, customised, or expanded to include new teams or geographies. This flexibility enables startups and mid-sized companies to operate with the efficiency of large enterprises, without bloating their finance departments While finance automation offers significant advantages, it also comes with challenges that businesses must navigate to ensure successful implementation. Also read: Strategies for Effective Procurement Risk Management Challenges in Finance Automation Finance automation can significantly improve efficiency, but it also brings several challenges. Understanding these common hurdles helps businesses prepare and implement effective solutions. Challenge What It Means Insight / Direction Initial Implementation Costs Automation platforms require upfront investment in tools, integration, and configuration. For mid-sized businesses, this can be a budget concern. Focus on ROI, not just cost. Platforms like Kodo offer modular features that let you start small and scale as needed. Change Management Employees may resist automation due to fear of job displacement or unfamiliarity with new tools. Lack of training delays adoption. Early team onboarding and role-specific training sessions help build confidence. Highlight time-saving benefits clearly. Data Security Automating financial workflows means handling sensitive data (vendor accounts, tax info, approvals). Breaches or leaks can result in significant financial and reputational losses. Select platforms that offer built-in access control, encryption, and audit trails. Kodo ensures enterprise-grade data protection. Integration Issues Integrating automation tools with legacy ERPs or accounting systems can be technically challenging and disrupt day-to-day operations if not done right. Use platforms that support open APIs and native integrations. Kodo integrates with leading ERPs, reducing friction. Also Read: 5 Signs Your Business Needs an Integrated Expense Management Solution Despite these challenges, the future of finance automation looks promising, with emerging technologies set to transform financial operations further. Wrapping Up From faster invoice processing to accurate vendor payments and real-time reporting, finance automation empowers businesses to operate with greater speed, accuracy, and control. By adopting intelligent automation platforms like Kodo , companies can eliminate repetitive tasks, reduce errors, and scale operations without increasing overhead. Whether you're a growing startup or an enterprise-level organisation, automation helps you gain full visibility into spending, ensure compliance, and improve overall financial health. More than 200 finance teams trust Kodo to manage their procure-to-pay spend efficiently and securely. Contact us to transform your financial workflows today! FAQs 1. What types of finance processes can be automated? You can automate invoice approvals, purchase orders, vendor payments, employee reimbursements, recurring subscriptions, budget tracking, and even tax filing workflows. 2. How does automation improve compliance and reduce risk? Automation ensures every financial transaction follows pre-defined rules and approval chains. It generates complete audit trails, validates GST or TDS entries, and reduces manual errors that often trigger compliance violations. 3. What is the ROI of investing in finance automation? Most businesses see ROI through reduced processing time, fewer errors, and cost savings on headcount and late fees. Automation also helps improve cash forecasting accuracy and overall financial efficiency. 4. How does automation help improve cash flow management? Automated systems schedule payments based on due dates and cash availability, prevent early or late payments, and provide real-time dashboards to monitor outflows, helping you plan working capital more effectively.

body_text: Press Flyme Auto Surpasses 3.14 Million Deployments Adds Over 143,000 New Deployments in June 2026 31.07.26 By ECARX The Company announced today the latest deployment milestone for Flyme Auto. In June 2026, Flyme Auto achieved over 143,000 new vehicle deployments, maintaining steady growth momentum. Cumulative deployments for the H1 2026 exceeded 880,000 vehicles. To date, the total number of vehicles equipped with Flyme Auto has surpassed 3.148 million, with the platform now deployed across over 50 production vehicle models from brands including Polestar, Geely Auto, Geely Galaxy and Lynk & Co, further expanding its intelligent cockpit footprint. The Company will continue to support the ongoing evolution of the Flyme platform and the full Flyme operating system portfolio, while accelerating development of its AI Agent-powered release. The all-new Flyme Auto 3.0 is scheduled to launch later this year, delivering enhanced intelligent cockpit experiences and next-generation AI capabilities. Flyme Auto is an intelligent cockpit operating system IP jointly developed by the Company and Meizu since 2023, based on Flyme OS. Combining consumer electronics innovation with automotive software expertise, Flyme Auto enables OEM partners to develop differentiated, brand-specific cockpit experiences through customizable operating systems. Following the execution of the definitive agreements for the Company’s acquisition of Flyme software business portfolio for RMB1.8 billion on June 18, 2026, the intellectual property rights related to Flyme OS and Flyme Auto are expected to be fully acquired by the Company.

title: Supio Alternatives
summary: Compare the top Supio alternatives for plaintiff law firms, including how Codes Health combines medical record retrieval, completeness review, and AI-powered analysis in a couple of weeks, not months.
body_text: When evaluating Supio alternatives, plaintiff law firms must determine whether they need a platform that analyzes records they already have or one that retrieves and analyzes records from the start. Supio has established itself as a capable AI legal document review platform, but many firms also need a solution for the upstream challenge: obtaining comprehensive medical records from providers. This guide examines the top Supio alternatives, with particular emphasis on how Codes Health combines medical record retrieval with AI-powered analysis, addressing the foundational retrieval step that document review platforms depend on. Key Takeaways Codes Health combines medical record retrieval, completeness review, and AI-powered legal analysis in one platform, addressing the workflow from provider outreach through litigation-ready insights Supio operates after records are obtained, while platforms like Codes Health handle both retrieval and analysis, making the two complementary for many workflows rather than direct competitors Retrieval timelines vary by provider, request complexity, and vendor. Some services report averages of 15 to 45 days, while Codes Health typically targets complete records in a couple of weeks Completeness verification matters. Codes Health's Missing Record Review is designed to identify gaps before demands or trial The Filevine partnership gives Codes Health native integration with a major case management platform, supporting workflows without context switching General-purpose AI tools like ChatGPT can analyze uploaded documents, but they aren't automatically validated for unsupervised, litigation-grade medical record review. Purpose-built platforms with human verification provide stronger safeguards Same-day digital retrieval may be limited to supported providers or available electronic sources. Firms should confirm whether any delivery includes the complete date range, billing records, imaging, and all relevant facilities What is Supio and Why Firms Seek Alternatives Supio positions itself as an AI legal document review platform covering the case lifecycle from intake to verdict. Supio Core Capabilities: AI-Generated Chronologies : Organizes existing medical records into timeline formats Demand Letter Drafting : Generates settlement demand packages from analyzed records Litigation Document Preparation : Creates complaints, motions, and deposition preparation materials Case Economics Analysis : Evaluates liens, expenses, and settlement valuations Conversation Intelligence : Provides insights from recorded case interactions Integrations : Thomson Reuters Westlaw Advantage, Litify, MyCase, and CasePeer Why Firms Look Elsewhere: Supio's official materials describe the platform working with records already brought into the system or supplied through connected systems and retrieval partners, rather than offering a native provider-retrieval service. Firms typically handle retrieval internally or use a separate service before Supio adds value, which is where the alternatives below come in, either as full replacements or as an upstream retrieval layer that feeds into Supio itself. Complementary Use Pattern: Some firms use a retrieval platform like Codes Health upstream, then route complete records to Supio for litigation drafting, covering the workflow from provider outreach through trial preparation. Understanding the Medical Record Retrieval Landscape Before examining the alternatives, it helps to understand how the market roughly divides, though the categories increasingly overlap: Category 1: AI Legal Document Review Platforms These platforms (Supio, EvenUp) primarily work with medical records you already have, focusing on generating litigation work product like demands, chronologies, and complaints, though some, like EvenUp's PLAAS service, now also offer retrieval-linked options. Category 2: Traditional Record Retrieval Services These vendors (National Record Retrieval, Ontellus, Lexitas, Compex) obtain records from providers, with varying levels of built-in analysis. Category 3: Combined Retrieval Plus Analysis This category (Codes Health, LlamaLab) handles both obtaining records and providing AI-powered insights. The key question for your firm: do you need a platform that analyzes records you already have, or do you need help obtaining complete records in the first place? For many plaintiff firms, upstream retrieval is a real bottleneck, since a demand letter platform can't add much value if a firm is missing critical treatment records. 1. Codes Health: Medical Record Retrieval and AI Analysis Platform Codes Health combines medical record retrieval, completeness review, and AI-powered legal analysis in one platform, which helps eliminate the need for firms to juggle separate retrieval and analysis vendors. For plaintiff law firms handling personal injury, mass torts, medical malpractice, workers' compensation, disability law, insurance litigation, and wrongful death cases, this combined capability supports pre-litigation operations end to end. Why Firms Choose Codes Health: Combined workflow coverage : Retrieval plus AI analysis in one solution, from provider outreach to litigation-ready chronologies Records targeted in a couple of weeks, not months : Codes Health's automated follow-ups and AI validation are built to work toward faster turnaround Case preparation support : AI-powered organization and insights extraction aimed at reducing manual review time Proactive completeness verification : Missing Record Review is designed to flag gaps before they become incomplete-evidence scenarios Core Platform Capabilities: Medical Record Retrieval : Connects through HIE integrations, TEFCA networks, EHR systems, provider portals, and traditional channels to gather medical, billing, and imaging records nationwide AI-Powered Case Chronologies : Automatically organizes and summarizes records chronologically, grouping patient encounters by visit for efficient review Insights Extraction Engine : Helps identify diagnoses, treatments, pre-existing conditions, missed appointments, care gaps, and documented future medical expenses Missing Record Review : Cross-references treatment timelines to flag gaps before demand preparation or trial Proactive Error Prevention : Incomplete or invalid authorizations are a common cause of rejection and delay. Missing signatures, expiration information, dates, or required permissions can require a request to be corrected and resubmitted. Applicable response deadlines vary by state and request pathway, while HIPAA generally allows up to 30 calendar days for an individual access request. Codes Health's AI review is designed to catch these issues before submission, automatically flagging misspellings, missing dates of service, and signature issues that would otherwise cause provider rejections The Filevine Strategic Partnership: Codes Health's partnership with Filevine is a significant advantage for firms using that case management platform. The native integration allows legal teams to submit retrieval requests directly from case files, track provider outreach in real time without leaving Filevine, communicate with the Codes Health team within the case workflow, receive completed records, billing, and imaging directly in the Filevine project, and review completeness status and retrieval history from a single interface. Flat-Fee Pricing Model: Codes Health operates on a flat-fee pricing structure. For high-volume firms, custom integrations with CRM platforms and other legal software are available. Continuous Platform Innovation: Codes Health's MIT-educated engineering team continuously builds out additional workflows and products, ensuring the platform constantly evolves, improves, and becomes more comprehensive to meet the changing demands of modern legal practices. What Legal Teams Are Saying: Charles Brown, Managing Partner at Daly & Black, P.C., noted that Codes Health is "technologically forward, using artificial intelligence in ways that none of the other providers could match." Kelman Harrel, Partner at Louis Law Firm, observed: "Wasted so much time, money, and energy on emerging technology. Codes Health has it dialed in." Best For: Plaintiff firms needing both record retrieval and AI analysis Teams seeking proactive gap identification before demands Filevine users wanting native workflow integration Firms looking to reduce the number of vendor relationships they manage Practices wanting to reduce the administrative work retrieval requires 2. EvenUp: Settlement Demand Generation, With Managed Retrieval Option EvenUp specializes in AI-enhanced settlement demand packages, focusing on the pre-litigation phase where many personal injury cases resolve. EvenUp Focus Areas: Demand Package Creation : Generates settlement demands Settlement Valuation : Uses AI to support case value assessments Pre-Litigation Optimization : Streamlined workflows for cases heading toward settlement Workflow Positioning: EvenUp's standalone drafting and chronology tools analyze case documents a firm already has, while its PLAAS managed service also includes medical record and bill retrieval. Firms should confirm which services are included in their specific EvenUp plan. Best For: Firms with high pre-litigation settlement volumes Teams seeking specialized demand generation, with or without managed retrieval 3. LlamaLab.ai: Speed-Focused Record Retrieval LlamaLab offers AI-native medical record retrieval with an emphasis on rapid turnaround, including same-day retrieval for some connected providers, along with provider discovery, authorization handling, and AI analysis. LlamaLab Features: Provider Discovery : Reverse search identifies treating providers AI Analysis : Analyzes medical documentation Multi-Channel Retrieval : Connects through various provider access points Bill Itemization : Organizes medical billing documentation Speed vs. Completeness Consideration: Same-day digital access may be limited to supported providers or available electronic sources. Firms evaluating any rapid-turnaround service, including LlamaLab, should confirm whether a delivery includes the complete date range, billing records, imaging, and all relevant facilities. Codes Health takes a different approach, working toward complete records in a couple of weeks with proactive gap identification through Missing Record Review. Best For: Firms prioritizing speed for initial record access Teams with robust internal processes for completeness verification 4. National Record Retrieval: Established Traditional Provider National Record Retrieval operates as a traditional medical record retrieval service with a flat-rate pricing model. National Record Retrieval Offerings: Nationwide Coverage : Retrieval services across all 50 states Flat Rate Pricing : No per-page charges Portal Integrations : Connects with Litify, Filevine, SmartAdvocate, and Law Ruler High Volume Capacity : Infrastructure for large case portfolios Service Model: National Record Retrieval focuses on obtaining records through traditional channels like phone, fax, email, and provider portals. The service handles outreach and follow-up but operates primarily as a retrieval vendor without built-in AI-powered analysis. Best For: Firms seeking established vendors Teams that handle analysis internally 5. RecordRS: Budget-Conscious Retrieval Option RecordRS offers transparent medical record retrieval with straightforward pricing, making it one of the more affordable options in the market. RecordRS Value Proposition: Transparent Pricing : Flat fee per request No Markup on Provider Fees : Provider charges passed through at cost Basic Retrieval Services : Core functionality for record acquisition Budget Trade-Offs: The lower price point reflects a focused service model. Firms choosing budget options should ensure they have internal capabilities for follow-up, completeness verification, and record analysis. Best For: Cost-conscious firms with strong internal operations Teams seeking simple, transparent pricing 6. Ontellus: Enterprise-Scale Retrieval Operations Ontellus serves enterprise clients requiring large-scale medical record retrieval operations. Ontellus Capabilities: Enterprise Infrastructure : Built for high-volume operations Nationwide Network : Established provider relationships Multiple Record Types : Medical, billing, and supporting documentation Pricing Structure: Ontellus promotes a simplified flat-fee SmartPricing model. Firms should request a current quote, since exact public rates and account-specific terms aren't publicly disclosed. Best For: Large firms with enterprise-scale needs Organizations requiring established vendor relationships 7. Lexitas Legal: Retrieval With Optional AI Chronology Analysis Lexitas Legal combines medical record retrieval with Record Insights, an AI-enabled medical chronology product available as an add-on. Lexitas Legal Services: Record Retrieval : Nationwide medical documentation acquisition with an average turnaround of 30 to 45 days and a reported 98% completion rate Record Insights : AI-enabled medical chronology service with introductory pricing starting at $0.25 per uploaded page Expanded Service Model: Lexitas positions itself as a large-scale legal support provider offering retrieval alongside optional AI-assisted chronology tools. Best For: Firms seeking established retrieval with an optional AI chronology add-on Teams handling high case volumes that value provider-relationship scale 8. Compex Legal Services: Retrieval With AI-Powered Summarization Compex Legal Services offers nationwide medical record retrieval as part of broader litigation support, including court reporting, and now includes Asabell, an AI-powered medical record summarization product. Compex Features: Nationwide Retrieval : Established coverage across all 50 states AI-Powered Summarization : Asabell provides AI-assisted medical record summaries Court Reporting : Additional litigation support services beyond retrieval Established Provider : Long-operating national retrieval vendor Best For: Firms seeking a traditional retrieval vendor with AI-assisted summarization bundled in Practices wanting court reporting and retrieval from a single provider Choosing the Right Platform: Decision Framework When to Choose Codes Health Select Codes Health when your firm needs: Combined workflow coverage : Both retrieval and AI analysis in one platform Proactive completeness verification : Missing Record Review works to identify gaps before they impact case outcomes Filevine integration : Native workflow within your existing case management system Turnaround measured in weeks, not months Reduced administrative burden : Codes Health manages provider outreach and follow-up once the required authorization and signatures are in place Practice-specific insights : AI tailored to personal injury, mass tort, and medical malpractice contexts When to Add Supio or EvenUp Consider adding these platforms when: You already have reliable, complete medical records You need AI-generated litigation documents like demands, complaints, and motions Your primary bottleneck is document drafting, not record retrieval You want to combine Codes Health's retrieval with downstream litigation tools When Traditional Retrieval May Fit Traditional vendors may suit firms that: Have robust internal analysis capabilities Prefer established vendor relationships Handle completeness verification and follow-up internally Why General AI Tools Have Limits for Medical Record Analysis Some firms consider using general-purpose AI platforms like ChatGPT for medical record review. General-purpose AI tools can analyze uploaded documents, summarize files, and answer questions about their contents, but they aren't automatically validated for unsupervised, litigation-grade medical record review and may produce errors or omit important context. Considerations for Firms: Accuracy : General AI models aren't specifically trained on medical-legal contexts, and outputs used in court-submitted documents generally require independent verification Compliance : Protected health information requires secure handling and clear audit trails; consumer use of general AI tools shouldn't automatically be assumed to meet these standards without confirming the applicable safeguards Context : Legal significance of clinical findings often requires specialized training that general-purpose tools weren't built around Codes Health's purpose-built AI combines automated processing with human verification, aiming for the "AI insights, verified by humans" standard litigation work calls for, tailored to personal injury, mass tort, and medical malpractice cases. Building Your Medical Record Technology Stack For Firms Using Filevine: The Codes Health plus Filevine integration is designed to support requests submitted directly from case files, AI-validated authorizations before submission, real-time provider outreach tracking, records delivered into the same project, AI-generated chronologies and insights for review, and routing to litigation drafting tools as needed. For High-Volume Practices: Codes Health offers custom integrations with CRM platforms and legal software for firms with significant case volumes, aiming to fit the platform into an existing technology ecosystem rather than requiring workflow changes. For Multi-Practice Firms: Codes Health serves seven legal practice areas with context-aware analysis tailored to each specialty: personal injury, mass torts, medical malpractice, workers' compensation, disability law, insurance litigation, and wrongful death. Frequently Asked Questions What are the primary differences between Supio and Codes Health? Supio operates as an AI legal document review platform that analyzes records you already have, generating demands, chronologies, and litigation documents. Codes Health addresses retrieval and completeness review, then provides AI-powered analysis. Many firms use Codes Health for retrieval and completeness verification, then route records to platforms like Supio for litigation drafting. The key distinction is that Supio generally assumes you have records, while Codes Health focuses on helping you get complete ones. How does integration with Filevine enhance the medical record retrieval process? The Codes Health and Filevine partnership embeds retrieval directly into your case management workflow. Legal teams can submit requests, track provider outreach, communicate with the Codes Health team, and receive completed records without leaving the relevant Filevine project, reducing context switching between vendor portals, email, and case files. Can AI solutions identify specific legal insights from complex medical records? Codes Health's Insights Extraction Engine is designed to identify diagnoses, treatments, pre-existing conditions, missed appointments, care gaps, and documented future medical expenses from unstructured records. The platform helps flag potential breaches in care and surface facts relevant to personal injury, mass tort, and medical malpractice litigation, with context-aware analysis tailored to specific practice areas. What security and compliance measures protect patient information? Codes Health operates as a HIPAA-compliant platform for handling protected health information. The service connects through health information exchanges, TEFCA networks, EHR systems, and provider portals with appropriate security controls. For Filevine users, the native integration is designed to keep data within established security frameworks. What should firms confirm when considering same-day retrieval services? Same-day digital retrieval typically relies on supported providers and available electronic sources, so firms should confirm whether a given delivery covers the complete requested date range, billing records, imaging, and all relevant facilities, rather than assuming speed and completeness go hand in hand. Codes Health manages provider outreach and follow-up after required authorization information is collected, working toward complete records in a couple of weeks and using Missing Record Review to help identify gaps before they affect case outcomes.

Her work ethos deeply resonates with our ambition to deliver high-quality production code for the teams that trust us, and our mission to grow the next generation of engineers. Her leadership wisdom and AI expertise will add a new dimension to what we’re building at GitStart, and we’re excited about the future.
